overall: Atlanta is running notably hotter than NWP models anticipated, with the current temperature and running max both sitting at 84.2°F as of 12:30 ET — already surpassing all three model forecasts (ECMWF 81.3, HRRR 82.1, NBM 81.0) by 2–3°F. Conditions are still warming at +1.8°F/hr with a very high dewpoint of 75.2°F, and the predicted peak hour is not until approximately 14:18 ET, leaving roughly 1.8 hours of potential additional warming. Broken cloud cover (62% at ~4,300 ft) may moderate but is unlikely to prevent further rises.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models are already busted low — observed temps have blown through their TMAX ceilings before the afternoon peak has even arrived. The models also called for peak timing around 11:00–12:00h, while observations and the timing model both point to a later peak near 14:18h, suggesting the models underestimated both the intensity and the duration of the warming window.
max_temp_prediction: With 84.2°F already locked in as the running max, ongoing warming at +1.8°F/hr, and roughly 1.8 hours left before the modeled peak, a simple projection yields around 87–88°F, though decelerating heating and partial cloud cover argue for the lower end of that range. The INTRADAY model places the highest probability in the 86–87°F bucket (36.4%), and a weighted expected value across INTRADAY probabilities lands near 86.5–87°F. Confidence is moderate-to-high that the final TMAX will be in the 86–88°F range, with the most likely outcome near 86.5°F.
